Empirical Research Plan:  “Do media‐only shocks move stock prices?  Evidence from the 5/4/1998 EntreMed frenzy”

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy:  Short-window Difference-in-Differences (DID) embedded in a classic event–study framework.

• Why DID?  
  – We have one clearly exogenous treatment date (the NYT front page on 5/3/1998, tradable on 5/4).  
  – A single firm is treated.  Without a control, a pure time–series event study cannot rule out synchronous market-wide shocks (e.g., a biotech rally).  
  – Constructing an untreated comparison group of similar biotechnology firms (plus broad-market indices) allows us to difference out such common shocks and attribute any residual jump in ENMD specifically to the media splash.  
  – The analysis can be replicated around the earlier Nature publication (11/28/1997 trading day) as a placebo.

Secondary strategy / robustness:  Synthetic-control and a market-model abnormal-return event study to verify the direction and size of the effect.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
   Treat_i = 1 if firm i is EntreMed, 0 otherwise.

Event window & timing  
   Post_t = 1 for trading days t ∈ [0, +2] relative to Monday 5/4/1998 (day 0).  
   Pre-period = trading days [-10, ‑3].  (We drop ‑2,-1 to avoid possible anticipatory leaks from the Sunday paper hitting some traders.)  
   Results are shown for alternative windows [-20,+20].

Control group  
   1. 10 nearest-neighbor public biotech firms matched on market cap and R&D intensity in 1997.  
   2. Nasdaq Biotech Index (NBI) constituents.  
   3. S&P 500 firms (broad market).  

Outcome variables  
   • Daily stock return, R_it.  
   • Abnormal return, AR_it = R_it – (α_i + β_i R_mkt,t) estimated in a one-year pre-event window.  
   • Log dollar trading volume.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends.  Conditional on time fixed effects, daily returns for ENMD would have moved like the control biotech firms absent the NYT story.  
      – Plausibility:  ENMD tracked peers closely during the 10-day and 20-day windows before the event; this can be visually inspected.

A2. No simultaneous fundamental information shocks.  
      – Institutional context stresses that the science was five months old; Lexis-Nexis search shows no SEC filings or patent announcements on 5/4.

A3. No anticipation within the estimation window.  
      – The NYT ran on Sunday (non-trading day), and it was not leaked earlier (verified by news wire search).

A4. Stable composition & no spillovers onto the control firms.  
      – Using multiple control groups dilutes any mild sector-wide halo.  We also test for spillovers directly (effect on controls).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Sector-wide excitement (spillover) after the NYT article.  
     → Include time fixed effects and market/sector returns; run a triple-difference dropping other angiogenesis-focused firms; quantify the abnormal return gap.

T2. Micro-structure issues (bid-ask bounce, price limits, thin trading).  
     → Use log-price change computed from mid-quotes where possible; replicate with 30‐minute intraday TAQ data as robustness.

T3. Post-event information arrival (learning that initial enthusiasm was overblown) could contaminate “post” period.  
     → Keep the post window extremely short (0, +1, +2 days).  Show that findings are robust when further shrinking the window to event-day-only.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)     # fast high-dim FE regressions
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
crsp <- fread("crsp_daily_1997_1998.csv")      # assume PERMNO, date, ret, vol, prc
mkt  <- fread("crsp_value_weighted_mkt_ret.csv")
matches <- fread("matched_biotech_permnos.csv") # columns: permno, match_group

# 2. Merge & construct variables --------------------------------------------
crsp <- merge(crsp, mkt, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)
crsp[, abnormal_ret := ret - (0.0 + 1.0)*vwretd ]  # placeholder; normally estimate α,β

# tag treated firm
ENMD_PERMNO <- 75090   # hypothetical
crsp[, treat := as.integer(permno == ENMD_PERMNO)]

# Event time in trading days relative to 1998-05-04
event_day <- as.Date("1998-05-04")
crsp[, rel_day := as.numeric(date - event_day)]
crsp[, post := as.integer(rel_day >= 0 & rel_day <= 2)]
crsp[, pre  := as.integer(rel_day >= -10 & rel_day <= -3)]

# Keep window
sample <- crsp[ (pre==1 | post==1) & (permno==ENMD_PERMNO | permno %in% matches$permno) ]

# 3. Main DID regression -----------------------------------------------------
did_mod <- feols(ret ~ treat*post + vwretd | permno + date, data = sample, cluster = "permno")
summary(did_mod)

# 4. Robustness: abnormal returns, alternative windows -----------------------
did_abn <- feols(abnormal_ret ~ treat*post | permno + date, data=sample, cluster="permno")
summary(did_abn)

# 5. Event-study plot --------------------------------------------------------
evt <- feols(ret ~ i(rel_day, treat, ref = -4) + vwretd | permno + date,
             data = crsp[permno==ENMD_PERMNO | permno %in% matches$permno],
             cluster = "permno")
iplot(evt)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Direction:  A sharply positive abnormal return for ENMD on the event day, well in excess of peers and market.  
• Magnitude:  ≈ +300 % raw (close-to-close) vs. ≈ 0 – 5 % for peers, so DID point estimate ≈ +300 p.p. on day 0.  
• We expect partial reversal within a week, consistent with a temporary media-driven mispricing.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel trends in pre-period ………………… 1  
C2: No anticipation …………………………………… 1  
C3: No simultaneous shocks ……………………… 0.5 (small chance of sector spillover)  
C4: Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers) … 0.5  
C5: Correct functional form / timing …………… 1  
Total = 4/5 → reasonably strong design, though sector spillovers remain the main caveat.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This plan combines the transparency of an event-study with the causal rigor of DID, leverages multiple control groups, and embeds several placebo and robustness checks to isolate the pure attention effect of media coverage on stock prices.
